prose: James Tillman separates two kinds of test-time scaling. The ordinary kind trades more compute for better results per task up to the compute used in training. 'Compute extrapolation' goes beyond training-level compute, and he thinks it likely speeds frontier progress, makes dangerous-capability evaluation harder and changes race dynamics. He sees it as newer and still being mastered through context management and multi-agent scaling, and argues it should be measured.
highlights: Distinction: scaling within vs beyond training compute
Extrapolation may speed progress and hinder safety evals
Improvements likely via context management, multi-agent setups
